one_liner: Integrate with Amazon to manage orders, catalog items, listings, and fulfillment.
auth_notes: Uses Login with Amazon (OAuth 2.0) to exchange refresh tokens for access tokens, plus AWS IAM / signature for requests.
access_notes: Requires developer registration and approval in the Solution Provider Portal to get working production credentials, though sandbox access is available.
api_notes: Extensive API covering orders, catalog, listings, FBA, pricing, reports, etc.
blocker_notes: Requires developer account registration and app approval.

auth.quote: To grant permission, selling partners follow an authorization flow based on Login with Amazon (LWA), which is Amazon's implementation of OAuth 2.0.

access.quote: Step 1. Register as an SP-API developer... You only need to register as a developer once, in any, to have continuous access to the SP-API. As part of registration, you must complete a Developer Profile.

reasons.auth: OAuth 2.0 is the only documented auth method for the SP‑API.
reasons.access: Developers can register an app and obtain sandbox credentials at no cost; production requires the same OAuth flow but no paid plan is needed to start building.
reasons.mcp: Amazon does not publish an MCP server for the SP‑API; only third‑party MCPs exist, so none_found.
reasons.verdict: Public documentation and free sandbox credentials allow a developer to build a working integration today.
